changes.before: Keep missing entries explicit in Scores and make scoreOrZero return a number without modifying the dictionary.
changes.after: Treat a missing dictionary entry as a real possibility.

before: An index signature [key: string] describes values read using string keys. In Scores, every lookup returns number | undefined. The explicit undefined is important: an arbitrary key may be absent, even when the compiler’s optional noUncheckedIndexedAccess setting is not enabled.

scoreOrZero takes a dictionary and key, reads scores[key], and uses typeof to check that the runtime value is a number. The runtime conditional test ? yes : no selects value when the test is true and zero otherwise. It returns that number or zero otherwise; a stored zero remains zero. JavaScript objects can inherit properties such as toString, so the runtime guard also prevents an inherited function from escaping as the promised number. This is a narrow numeric check, not complete external-data validation. The example prints 8 and 0.
Optional local practice: Call with the art key and explain why a zero result does not prove the property was absent.
after: A dictionary stores values under keys. An index signature describes the values read with those keys. Here, `[key: string]: number | undefined` says a text-key lookup may give a number or no value.

ScoreOrZero reads the chosen entry and checks whether it is a number. The `? :` expression chooses between that number and zero. Checking the actual value also prevents an inherited function, such as toString, from being returned as a number.
The art entry really contains 0. It stays 0. A zero result therefore does not tell you whether the key existed or the backup was used.
An arbitrary lookup cannot be assigned straight to a number-only variable because it might be undefined. Keep absence in the type and handle it in the code.

after.question: Why can an arbitrary Scores lookup fail when assigned directly to a number-only variable?

project.title: Admit that a dictionary entry can be missing
project.task: Return a numeric score or zero while keeping missing entries explicit in the type.
